newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees 11.6 pct accumulated inflation in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees 11.6 pct accumulated inflation in 1996.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet forecast 11.6 percent accumulated inflation for this year, up from 10.2 percent in 1995.
Accumulated inflation in the first eight months of 1996 was 8.84 percent, compared with 7.3 percent in the same period last year.
Speaking to Congress, Camet added that inflation in 1997 should be around nine percent as estimated in the budget.

He also said the 1997 budget estimate for an average exchange rate of 2.70 soles to the dollar would "allow a small increase in the exchange rate in real terms." The sol traded today at 2.485 to the dollar.

The government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had agreed an accumulated inflation goal for 1996 of between 9.5 percent and 11.5 percent. Peru's 1995 inflation of 10.2 percent was the country's lowest in 23 years.
